title: One chart, one sentence
concept:
The last step turns a correct table into something a manager acts on. A hiring test marks three decisions.

**1. The right chart for the question.**
- Comparing categories (regions, reps, channels): **columns or bars**, sorted largest first, so the ranking reads at a glance.
- Change over time (months, quarters): a **line**, left to right in time order. Never sort time by value.
- A pie only for a few parts of one whole (two or three slices). Past that, readers can't compare the angles.

**2. A title that states the finding.** "Revenue by region" describes the axes; "Macedonia now brings in the most revenue" tells the reader what to take away. Highlight the bar the title is about, and leave the rest quiet.

**3. One sentence with the number.** Who or what, how much, compared with what: "In Qtr4, X brought in €Y, Z% of the quarter's revenue."

> [!excel] Click the pivot ▸ PivotTable Analyze ▸ **PivotChart**. It stays linked: refresh the pivot and the chart follows. Chart Design ▸ Change Chart Type; click the title to type your finding. Sheets: select the pivot ▸ Insert ▸ Chart.

worked.prompt: How did revenue move month by month?

story.title: Revenue peaked in March and slumped in August

worked.explain: Month in Rows (Date grouped by Months), Sum of Revenue; a line, in month order. The title says what happened, not what's plotted. Press the button to build it in the lab.

mistakes: A pie with five or more slices: bars compare sizes far better.
Sorting quarters or months by value: time must stay in order.
An axis-label title ("Revenue by region"). Say the finding.
A sentence with no number, or a number with no comparison.

drills.ask: Show how **total revenue moved across the year**, quarter by quarter: build the pivot, pick the right chart and order. Then press **Check**.
drills.hint: Rows: Date → Quarters, Sum of Revenue. Change over time → a line (or columns), kept in quarter order.

drills.ask: Compare the **regions' full-year revenue** so the leader jumps out: the right chart, the right order, and a title that states the finding. Then press **Check**.
drills.hint: Rows: Region, Sum of Revenue. Columns or bars, largest first. The title names the region that leads.

story.title: Attica brought in the most revenue in 2025

drills.ask: Which **channel** earned the most **Margin**? Pivot it, chart it, and finish the sentence. Then press **Check**.

story.sentence: {top} earned the most margin: €{amount}, {share}% of all margin.

drills.hint: Rows: Channel, Values: Margin (Sum). For the share, switch Show Values As to % of Grand Total, read it, and round to one decimal.

questions.prompt: Revenue for each of 12 months, to show the trend. Best chart?
questions.explain: Change over time is a line in time order. Sorting months by value hides the trend.
A finding says what the reader should take away. The others only label the axes.

questions.prompt: A bar chart of five regions' revenue: why sort it largest first?
options: So the ranking reads at a glance
questions.explain: Sorting changes nothing in the data; it puts the answer where the eye starts.

claimAfter: I can pick the right chart, title it with the finding, and write the one-sentence insight.
notYet: You haven't done it all end to end on messy data yet: that's Assignment 3. Doing it against the clock is the mock test.
